title: Zero-energy bound state trapped in line-shaped vortex in topological superconductor
abstract: Fermion bound states in the core of a line-shaped vortex of a two-dimensional topological superconductor are investigated. The superconducting pairing potential, described in terms of elliptical coordinates, vanishes along a line defect with the two foci at the endpoints. The superconductivity is induced into a topological insulator via proximity effect with a type II s-wave superconductor. The spin and the momentum are perpendicularly locked by the strong spin-orbit coupling via Rashba interaction. A zero-energy Majorana state arises from the Berry phase together with a sequence of equally spaced fermion exitations. By solving the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations using the method employed by Caroli, de Gennes and Matricon we calculate the energies, the wave-functions and spin-polarization of the bound states. An analytic expression for the local density of states within the vortex is obtained.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes the bound states trapped in a line-shaped vortex within a 2D topological superconductor. By solving the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations using elliptical coordinates, the authors predict the existence of a zero-energy Majorana state and quantized excited states. The findings provide crucial theoretical predictions for detecting topologically protected quantum phenomena in superconducting materials.
main_problem: The study investigates zero-energy fermion bound states trapped within a line-shaped vortex core of a two-dimensional topological superconductor.
main_result: A zero-energy Majorana state is predicted to exist, alongside equally spaced excited states whose energies are determined by solving the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations in elliptical coordinates.
method: The analysis involves solving coupled differential equations derived from the BdG formalism using specialized techniques suited for line defects, including matching solutions across different radial regimes.
model_or_system:
The system is a 2D electron gas on a topological insulator surface, subjected to proximity-induced s-wave superconductivity and Rashba spin-orbit coupling. The geometry necessitates the use of elliptical coordinates $(\mu, 
u)$ due to the line-shaped vortex.
key_observables: Zero-energy Majorana state ($E_0=0$), quantized excited state energies ($E_m$), and the Local Density of States (LDOS) measured via STM.
important_parameters: The superconducting gap $\Delta(r)$ vanishes along the line defect ($\mu=0$); parameters include Fermi velocity ($v_F$) and coupling strengths.

why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework for predicting robust zero-energy modes (Majorana fermions) in superconducting topological systems, which is highly relevant to realizing topological quantum computation platforms.
